standard_prerequisites.name: Characterization of cartesian and cocartesian squares by exactness
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the translation of cartesianness and cocartesianness of the square into exactness of the displayed sequence through the direct sum, applied in both directions in the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Kernels and cokernels in a cartesian square
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the morphism induced on the kernels of the two horizontal maps is an isomorphism, which produces the epimorphism in the last step.

standard_prerequisites.name: Characterizations of monomorphisms and epimorphisms
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the isomorphism obtained from the previous lemma into the statement that the relevant morphism is an epimorphism.

core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 1124-1131): with u and v the two maps through the direct sum, the hypothesis makes v an epimorphism, so by the characterization lemma the displayed four-term sequence is exact; the characterization lemma applied once more makes the square cocartesian, and the last assertion follows from the lemma on kernels in a cartesian square together with the characterization of epimorphisms.
Part (2) (proof line 1132): the dual assertion follows by duality.
proof_roadmap: Turn cartesianness into exactness of the sequence through the direct sum.
Use the epimorphism hypothesis to extend the exactness to the last term.
Read off cocartesianness and the epimorphism on the kernels, then dualize.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a cartesian square with an epimorphism in the lower horizontal map is cocartesian with an epimorphism in the upper horizontal map, and dually that a cocartesian square with a monomorphism in the left vertical map is cartesian with a monomorphism in the right vertical map (statement lines 1103-1121). The proof is a complete argument: the two maps through the direct sum are formed and the hypothesis gives an exact four-term sequence, which yields cocartesianness and, through the kernel lemma, the remaining epimorphism statement (proof lines 1124-1131); the second assertion is dual (proof line 1132). The non-formal content is the two applications of the characterization through the direct sum. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
